Fix macOS ICMP traceroute 100% packet loss (v0.11.1)

DGRAM ICMP sockets cannot receive ICMP Time Exceeded messages from
intermediate routers - they only receive Echo Reply messages. This
caused all hops to show as `* * *` with 100% loss.

Fix: Use RAW socket for receiving (can receive all ICMP types) while
keeping DGRAM for sending (supports IP_TTL per-packet). This requires
sudo on macOS since RAW sockets need root privileges.

Fix IPv6 ICMP traceroute on Linux

Linux delivers ICMPv6 Echo Reply only to the socket that sent the
request. Since ttl uses separate send/receive sockets, the receiver
never saw Echo Reply packets, causing 100% packet loss at the
destination hop.

Fix:
- Add poll_ipv6_echo_reply() to drain Echo Reply from send socket
- Use correct ICMPv6 Echo Request type 128 (was incorrectly type 8)
- Enable IPV6_RECVHOPLIMIT on send socket for asymmetry detection
- Linux-only (#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]) - macOS unaffected

Intermediate hops (Time Exceeded) were always delivered correctly
to any raw ICMPv6 socket; only destination detection was broken.

Fix ICMPv6 checksum computation for IPv6 traceroute

IPv6 traceroute was not detecting destinations because ICMPv6 packets
had invalid checksums. The kernel was expected to fill in the checksum
for raw ICMPv6 sockets but did not. Destinations dropped packets with
checksum 0, while intermediate hops (Time Exceeded) still worked because
routers don't validate the original ICMP checksum.

Changes:
- Add icmp_ipv6_checksum() function implementing RFC 8200 pseudo-header
  checksum (algorithm derived from trippy, BSD-licensed)
- Update build_echo_request() to accept source/dest addresses for IPv6
- Bind IPv6 sockets to source IP for checksum consistency
- Handle binding edge cases (unspecified addresses, graceful failures)
- Add debug_assert to catch callers forgetting IPv6 addresses
- Add known-value checksum test from trippy fixtures

Fix macOS probe TTL batching issue (#12)

On macOS, rapid setsockopt(IP_TTL) + send() calls get batched by the
kernel, causing multiple probes to be sent with the same TTL value.
This resulted in only 1 hop being displayed.

Fix: Add 200µs minimum delay between probes on macOS (when --rate is
not specified) to ensure each set_ttl() takes effect before the next
send().

Root cause analysis from pcap: First 17 probes all sent with IP TTL=17,
then TTL 18-30 worked correctly. Destination reply to seq 256 (TTL 1
encoded) caused dest_ttl=1 to be set, locking subsequent rounds to
TTL=1 only.

Fix macOS single-hop traces: per-probe send sockets for ICMP/UDP/TCP (#12)

On macOS, sendto() is asynchronous: the kernel stamps each queued datagram
with the socket's current IP_TTL at drain time, not at the sendto() call. A
tight setsockopt(IP_TTL); send loop on a shared socket could therefore emit
every probe with the final TTL, collapsing the trace to a single hop —
intermittently, and more often on fast Apple Silicon. The prior 500us
inter-probe delay only masked this and was insufficient on some hardware.

Each probe is now sent from a fresh socket on macOS across all three modes:
- ICMP: per-probe socket; shared socket retained for PMTUD + Linux echo poll.
- UDP: per-probe socket re-bound to the flow source port (SO_REUSEADDR,
  macOS-only) so Paris/Dublin flow ID and NAT detection are preserved.
- TCP: per-probe raw socket; source port lives in the crafted SYN.

A macOS preflight creates/binds the socket(s) once before the loop so a
misconfiguration fails fast instead of spinning. Other platforms are
unchanged; the 500us delay is kept as a margin and for the FreeBSD/NetBSD raw
paths. Correlation is unaffected (receiver matches on sequence /
payload-embedded id, not the kernel ICMP identifier).

Roadmap: track TTL send-path correctness follow-ups before next release

Three follow-ups to the macOS single-hop fix (#12): convert the FreeBSD/NetBSD
raw send paths to per-probe sockets, drop the now-redundant macOS arm of the
500us inter-probe delay, and (subsuming both) optionally unify the send path on
IP_HDRINCL so the TTL is written into the IP header instead of via setsockopt.

Unify IPv4 send path on IP_HDRINCL (TTL in the IP header) (#12)

Send every IPv4 probe through a single raw IP_HDRINCL socket with the TTL
written into a hand-built IP header, instead of setsockopt(IP_TTL) before an
asynchronous sendto. This removes the stale-TTL race behind #12 by
construction, uniformly across platforms — no per-probe sockets, no inter-probe
delay for IPv4. IPv6 is unchanged (no IPv4-style IP_HDRINCL for v6).

New probe::rawip module builds the IPv4 header (per-OS ip_len/ip_off byte
order: host on macOS/NetBSD, network on Linux/FreeBSD>=11), the UDP datagram +
checksum, and the IP_HDRINCL socket; one socket emits ICMP/UDP/TCP via the
protocol byte. DSCP maps to ToS; PMTUD sets DF in the header (also fixing IPv4
PMTUD on NetBSD). --source-ip binds the socket so a non-local source fails
fast. Response correlation is unchanged.

Validated by unit tests (checksums, header layout, both byte-order branches),
a privileged real-kernel send test wired into the Linux/macOS/FreeBSD CI jobs
(each validates its own ip_len/ip_off byte order; macOS covers NetBSD's
host-order branch), and a Linux on-wire test that verifies the emitted TTL,
ToS, protocol, addresses, and checksums.

IPv6: per-probe sockets on FreeBSD/NetBSD; remove inter-probe delay (#12)

NetBSD for the IPv6 path, so a fast BSD host can no longer collapse an IPv6 trace
to a single hop (issue #12). There is no IPv4-style IP_HDRINCL for IPv6, so a
fresh socket per probe is the deterministic fix.

A new build.rs defines the per_probe_send cfg (macOS/FreeBSD/NetBSD) as the

shared socket (its sendto never raced).

With IPv4 on IP_HDRINCL and IPv6 per-probe across all BSD-derived platforms, the
rapid probe sweeps are race-free, so the 500us apply_rate_limit floor is removed;

fix: parse IPv6 extension headers in quoted error payloads (LAN-144) (#114)

* fix: parse IPv6 extension headers in quoted error payloads (LAN-144)

ICMPv6 error messages (Time Exceeded, Dest Unreachable, Packet Too Big)
quote the original IPv6 packet that triggered the error. If the quoted
packet contains extension headers (Hop-by-Hop, Routing, Dest Options),
the transport header (ICMPv6/UDP/TCP) starts after byte 40, not at it.

Previously, parse_icmp_error_payload_v6_dgram and the raw-socket
parse_icmp_error_payload_v6_with_mtu sliced at a fixed 40-byte offset,
mis-aligning the transport header and mis-correlating probes.

New helper skip_ipv6_ext_headers_quoted walks extension headers in the
quoted IPv6 data and returns (transport_offset, final_next_header).
Fragment headers and unsupported protocols (ESP, AH) are rejected.

Fixes both the active DGRAM path and the raw-socket path.

Closes LAN-144.

fix: bound enrichment caches to prevent unbounded memory growth (LAN-145) (#115)

Add prune_cache helper in lookup/mod.rs that performs two-phase eviction:
1. Drop TTL-expired entries (cached_at + ttl has elapsed)
2. If still over ENRICHMENT_CACHE_CAP (10,000), evict oldest by cached_at

Apply to all four enrichment caches:
- ASN (src/lookup/asn.rs): prune after insert in lookup()
- rDNS (src/lookup/rdns.rs): prune after insert in reverse_lookup()
- Geo (src/lookup/geo.rs): prune after insert in lookup()
- IX (src/lookup/ix.rs): prune after insert in lookup(), merge dual
  ip_cache + ip_cache_times maps into single HashMap<IpAddr, IpCacheEntry>
  to eliminate the dual-map sync hazard and simplify eviction

CAP rationale: 64 max TTL × ~3 responders/hop × 10 targets = ~2,000 IPs.
10,000 gives 5× headroom while preventing pathological growth.

fix: populate response TTL on macOS/BSD IPv4 (1-byte IP_RECVTTL cmsg) (#117)

The cmsg length gate added when hardening the unsafe cmsg parser required
CMSG_LEN(size_of::<c_int>()). That is right for Linux IPv4 IP_TTL and the
IPv6 hop-limit (both arrive as a 4-byte int), but the BSDs and macOS deliver
the IPv4 IP_RECVTTL value as a single u_char. Its cmsg is CMSG_LEN(1), which
fell under the gate and was dropped, so response_ttl came back None and the
return-hop / path-asymmetry estimate derived from it went blank on those
platforms.

Read the value width-aware: require at least one data byte, read a 4-byte int
when the payload is >= 4 bytes, otherwise the single byte. This keeps the
short-cmsg over-read protection while restoring the 1-byte case.

Adds a regression test that feeds a synthetic 1-byte and 4-byte cmsg (the
1-byte case returned None before, Some after) and covers the empty-payload
skip; it runs the platform-specific cmsg_type branches under their real cfg
on the macOS and FreeBSD CI runners.

The dirty-skip fingerprint relied on hop_mut()/reset_stats() to bump

the next dirty frame — up to 2s (the rate-limit worker's tick) when
paused or in a finished replay. Treat a Resize event as invalidating
the last fingerprint so the next tick redraws.
